children: Shares of PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar, crashed 30 per cent in Thursday's session, hitting an 18-month low after the stock touched back-to-back lower circuits.

The shares of PB Fintech quoted at Rs 1,320.10 apiece on the NSE, down 30.02 per cent. The stock had closed at Rs 1,886.30 in the previous session, after gaining more than 8 per cent in a three-day rally.
The sharp decline came after the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) proposed a sweeping overhaul of insurance distribution economics.

Mayank Jain, Market Analyst, Share.Market by PhonePe, said the decline reflects market concerns over proposed caps on distributor commission structures, including reducing health insurance payouts to 15-20 per cent and term life commissions to 25 per cent.
These proposals could squeeze PB Fintech's take-rates, lower operating margins and disrupt its core tele-calling lead generation model, he said.
"From a trading perspective, market participants remain cautious in the short term, avoiding rapid entries until the stock stabilises and establishes a clear technical floor," Jain said.
Existing retail investors are evaluating whether to avoid selling at distressed levels, as the consultation paper remains a draft open for public and industry feedback through late October, he added.

"Market observers are watching for management commentary and regulatory clarity before evaluating fresh long positions, while long-term positions depend on how effectively PB Fintech can recalibrate its customer acquisition costs and pivot toward lower-cost digital distribution channels," Jain said.

PB Fintech's business model will be under focus as the company faces proposed cuts in health renewal and porting commissions, first-year term life commissions, and motor own-damage and third-party commissions, Emkay Global said.
The proposed commission cuts are far more severe than expected and PB Fintech is likely to be the most impacted, Bernstein said.
The proposed take-rate caps could materially pressure PB Fintech's unit economics, particularly in health and motor insurance, Bernstein added.
Near-term stock moves could reflect pressure on PB Fintech from the larger-than-expected commission cuts, it said.
